## Round 1 (gen 1) findings
- q19 is the only visible template (TPC-H Q19 shape: OR of 3 branches, each with join eq + part preds + lineitem preds). Baseline ~307ms hot.
- E0001 ACCEPTED (-46%): JoinDependentFilterRule (src/optimizer/rule/join_dependent_filter.cpp) only fires on ROOT OR; DistributivityRule factored the join eq out first. Fixed by reordering in optimizer.cpp.
- ExpressionRewriter::ApplyRules: is_root=true only on top call from VisitExpression. Rewriter runs once per optimization.
- dbe-tool sql cannot run shell loops/pipes/variables; run single statements (grep pipe on output OK). Single-run timings noisy.

## Round 2 (gen 1)
- E0002 ACCEPTED (-38%): the OR-of-ranges on l_quantity is an EXPRESSION_FILTER (not ConjunctionOr). Dense mask eval + gather in column_segment.cpp TryDenseFilterSelection. Lesson: check which TableFilterType actually reaches FilterSelection before optimizing.
- Scan filter loop: RowGroup::Scan (row_group.cpp ~760) applies filters in AdaptiveFilter order, then Select()s the other columns with sel.
- BFTableFilter (planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp) is a simple blocked BF; looked fine.

## Round 3 (gen 1) - current best 168.7ms q19 (2.996x)
- Profile: lineitem TABLE_SCAN 3.38s cumulative of 0.478s wall; still dominant. Part scan+filter ~0.13s; join 0.01s.
- Storage: l_shipinstruct/l_shipmode = VARCHAR Dictionary (plain, NOT dict_fsst) + VALIDITY Constant; l_partkey BIGINT BitPacking, l_quantity DECIMAL BitPacking.
- Microbench: count(*) WHERE l_shipinstruct=const -> 1.14s cumulative, 0.154s wall (~1/3 of the q19 scan).
- Key code fact: StandardColumnData::Filter (standard_column_data.cpp:76) uses the segment's compression->filter only if both data and validity compressions have one; otherwise ColumnData::Filter = full scan + per-row FilterSelection. Plain Dictionary (dictionary_compression.cpp:170) has NO filter; DictFSST has DictFSSTFilter (dict_fsst.cpp:180), which evaluates on the dictionary once and caches filter_result. Constant validity has ConstantFilterValidity (numeric_constant.cpp:178); its FiltersNullValues switch throws on unknown filter types.
- Dictionary scan: CompressedStringScanState (storage/compression/dictionary/decompression.cpp) builds a reusable dictionary in Initialize and emits a dict vector for full 2048-row scans.
- Dispatched: Dictionary-level filter for plain Dictionary segments.

## Next ideas
- If the dict filter lands: re-profile; the remaining scan cost is probably the BitPacking decode of partkey/quantity plus the BF dynamic filter. Consider adaptive filter order (is the shipinstruct dict filter applied first?).

- Part side: the 2M-row part scan + FILTER with OR of string preds costs 0.08s; the dict filter may help if part columns are Dictionary too (check pragma_storage_info('part')).
- Follow-up from E0002: building ConjunctionOr-of-And TableFilters for OR-of-ranges would enable zonemap pruning (riskier).
- The backlog issue on optional IN in scan is mostly subsumed by the dict filter issue.

issues.title: Dictionary-level filter evaluation for Dictionary-compressed string segments
issues.hypothesis: The q19 lineitem TABLE_SCAN is still ~90% of the query (3.38s cumulative of 0.478s wall). l_shipinstruct and l_shipmode are stored with plain `Dictionary` compression and `Constant` validity (pragma_storage_info). An isolated `count(*) FROM lineitem WHERE l_shipinstruct='DELIVER IN PERSON'` costs 1.14s cumulative, about a third of the q19 scan. DictionaryCompressionFun::GetFunction (src/storage/compression/dictionary_compression.cpp:170) registers no `filter` callback. So StandardColumnData::Filter (standard_column_data.cpp:76) takes the fallback ColumnData::Filter: it emits a dictionary vector, then ColumnSegment::FilterSelection compares strings row by row through the dictionary sel (17-byte constant, so no inlined fast compare). DictFSST already has the fix (DictFSSTFilter, dict_fsst.cpp:180): evaluate the filter once on the dictionary entries (a handful per segment here), cache a bool per entry, then map each row via the dictionary sel. The Constant validity segment already has a filter (ConstantFilterValidity, numeric_constant.cpp:178), so once Dictionary has a filter the fast path will be taken.
issues.plan:
1. In src/include/duckdb/storage/compression/dictionary/decompression.hpp, add to CompressedStringScanState: `unsafe_unique_array<bool> filter_result;` and `bool null_filter_result_initialized = false;` (mirror the dict_fsst scan state).
2. In src/storage/compression/dictionary_compression.cpp, add `DictionaryCompressionStorage::StringFilter(ColumnSegment&, ColumnScanState&, idx_t vector_count, Vector &result, SelectionVector &sel, idx_t &sel_count, const TableFilter&, TableFilterState&)`, ported from DictFSSTFilter:
   - Only when vector_count == STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE and the dictionary was initialised.
   - Lazily build filter_result[dictionary_size] by running ColumnSegment::FilterSelection on `Vector(dictionary->data, 1, dictionary_size)` (slot 0 is NULL).
   - Unpack the bitpacked selection into sel_vec exactly as ScanToDictionaryVector does (including the start_offset shift).
   - Loop over the incoming sel (sel_count rows): idx = sel_vec[row]; slot 0 → evaluate the NULL entry lazily as DictFSST does; keep the row if filter_result[idx].
   - Write a new sel only if some rows were dropped. Set `result.Dictionary(dictionary, *sel_vec)` so later columns and the output still see the dictionary vector.
   - Otherwise fall back to StringScan + FilterSelection.
3. Register the filter. The CompressionFunction constructor has trailing optional args, so set `res.filter = ...` after construction (as dict_fsst.cpp:295 does).
4. Correctness guard: cache filter_result only when the filter tree (recurse through CONJUNCTION_AND/OR and OPTIONAL children) has no DYNAMIC_FILTER, BLOOM_FILTER or other filter whose result can change during the scan. For those, re-evaluate on the dictionary every vector (still cheap, since the dictionary is small), or fall back.
5. Check that ConstantFun::FiltersNullValues (numeric_constant.cpp:110) does not throw for any filter type that can now reach it on VARCHAR columns. Its default case throws InternalException; add the missing cases if needed (e.g. DYNAMIC_FILTER → filters_nulls=true conservatively is wrong; use filters_nulls=false, filters_valid_values=false, which keeps everything and is safe because the data filter already ran).
Verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE count(*) WHERE l_shipinstruct = const (expect well below 1.14s cumulative) and with bench q19.
issues.expected_gain: q19 -15..-25%: the shipinstruct equality is about 1/3 of scan CPU, and the optional shipmode IN on the same storage type also gets cheaper.
issues.generality: Any scan with a pushed-down filter (equality, IN, range, LIKE-as-expression filter) on a low-cardinality VARCHAR column stored with plain Dictionary compression, which is very common in TPC-H/TPC-DS (flags, modes, statuses, categories). Regression case: a dictionary nearly as large as the vector (high-cardinality segment), where per-entry evaluation duplicates work. Bound it by taking the path only when dictionary_size <= vector_count, or let it be since it is amortised over the segment.
issues.risk: Medium. Storage filter path: needs correct NULL slot-0 handling, the bitpacking start_offset shift, no stale cache for dynamic filters, and FiltersNullValues coverage. The DictFSST implementation is a proven template.
